name: Runner's Logic
description: A neural-feed serialized drama following the rotating members of a mid-tier runner crew operating in the corridor between Tier 2 and Tier 3 GLMZ, taking contracts that range from data extraction to physical courier work in corponation-restricted zones. The show is distinguished by its procedural accuracy — production consultants with runner backgrounds designed the immersion sequences — and its refusal to romanticize the work's physical and psychological toll. The audience inhabits a different crew member each episode, including support roles that never leave the safe house.
cultural_impact: The show's support-role episodes — particularly the 'logistics' and 'medic' episodes — shifted cultural perception of runner crews from lone-operator mythology to a more complex understanding of collective interdependence.
story_hooks: The production consultant who designed the immersion sequences has gone dark; the last message they sent to the showrunner said they recognized something in their own work that they didn't put there.

A real runner crew has begun structuring their actual operations around the show's fictional protocols — either because the show is that accurate, or because someone fed the writers real operational data as a test.

Episode 19 of Season 3, which depicts a failed extraction resulting in a crew member's death, was pulled from the feed 48 hours after release with no explanation; physical copies are circulating on the Shelf.
